label: The training will likely complete successfully with a train_time between 700,000 and 900,000 ms, continuing the trend of decreasing training time observed in prior experiments (record_5: 949,528 ms; record_4: 1,301,740 ms; record_3: 1,386,147 ms). The distributed Muon optimizer introduced in this version parallelizes the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization across GPUs, reducing per-step compute. Hyperparameters (num_iterations=5100, batch sizes, learning rate) match record_5, so total steps are identical. The order change of QK norm and rotary embedding is unlikely to affect speed.
reason: Prior experiments show a consistent reduction in train_time as optimizations (Muon, rotary embeddings, QK norm, distributed data loading) are added. The current code adds distributed support to Muon (splitting parameter updates across ranks and all-reducing), which should further reduce per-iteration compute time. Syntax is valid per deterministic evidence. Risks include potential communication overhead from all-reducing a ~168 MB bfloat16 tensor across GPUs, but compute reduction likely dominates.
confidence_reason: High confidence due to strong directional trend across five prior runs and a clear optimization (distributed Muon) that targets the main compute bottleneck. Uncertainty remains because the exact GPU count (world_size) and network bandwidth are unknown, and the all-reduce could become a bottleneck if the cluster is not high-bandwidth.
